summary: Changhwan Park is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Otani University and UC Berkeley (Ph.D.) under Alexander von Rospatt, Noritoshi Aramaki, and Shoryu Katsura. He served as a professor at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2017).

Channa Li is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied under Jonathan A. Silk (attested 2015). She holds a post as Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Chao-heng Liao works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He has held positions at Academia Sinica (attested 2018) and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies as an adjunct researcher (attested 2026).

Charlene E. Makley is an anthropologist of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Michigan in 1999 under Norma Diamond and Roy Rappaport, later becoming associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.

Charles A. Moore (1901–1967) was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Yale (A.B. 1926, Ph.D. 1932). He taught at Yale and served as professor at the University of Hawaiʻi (1936–1967), founding and editing Philosophy East and West.
Charles Alfred Bell (1870–1945) was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics who studied at Winchester College (~1884–1889) and New College (~1889–1891).

Charles B. Jones is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia (1996) under Paul Groner. He served as an Associate Professor and Associate Dean at the Catholic University of America.

Charles Bally (1865–1947) was a linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1886–1889) and under Ferdinand de Saussure (~1893–1913). He was on the faculty at the University of Geneva from approximately 1893 to 1939.

Charles Burnett (born 1951) is a scholar of history, archaeology, philosophy, and Indology. He earned his BA and doctorate at Cambridge and held posts at the University of Sheffield and the Warburg Institute, where he became a professor in 1999.

Charles Cutler Torrey (1863–1956) was a scholar of religious studies, history, and linguistics who studied under Theodor Nöldeke. He taught Semitic languages at Andover Theological Seminary (1892–1900) and was a professor at Yale University (1900–1932).

Charles D. Orzech is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies who completed his dissertation at the University of Chicago. He chaired the Religious Studies Department at UNC Greensboro (attested 1998–2006) and was a National Humanities Center Fellow.

Charles DiSimone is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held academic posts at the University of Munich (attested 2021) and Ghent University (attested 2026), where he is a co-director and permanent member.

Charles Duroiselle (1871–1951) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He served at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, taught Pali at the University of Rangoon, and was Superintendent of the Archaeological Survey of Burma (1912–1940).

Charles Edmund Godakumbura (1907–1977) was an Indologist and historian who earned multiple degrees, including a Ph.D. and D.Litt., from the University of London. He taught at SOAS (~1953–1959) and served as Commissioner of Archaeology for the Archaeological Survey of India.

Charles Eliot (1862–1931) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology educated at Cheltenham College and Balliol College, Oxford. He worked for the Foreign Office (~1886–1926) and served as principal of the University of Hong Kong (~1912–1918).

Charles Elliott (1776–1856) was active in Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts with the East India Company and served as Treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

Charles Gabriel Seligman (1873–1940) studied medicine at St Thomas' Hospital Medical School (~1892–1896). He held the chair of Ethnology jointly at the London School of Economics and the University of London from 1913 to 1934.

Charles Goodman specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan in 2002 under Allan Gibbard and became an Associate Professor at Binghamton University (attested 2013).

Charles H. Long (1926–2020) was a religious studies scholar who earned his B.D. and Ph.D. from the University of Chicago, later serving as assistant dean. He held faculty posts at UNC Chapel Hill, Duke, Syracuse, and UC Santa Barbara.

Charles Hallisey (born 1953) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Colgate, Harvard Divinity School, Pennsylvania, and Chicago (Ph.D. ~1988). He has held faculty posts at Loyola University Chicago, Wisconsin-Madison, and Harvard University.
